title: ÆON Learn canonical semantic lesson
description: The one canonical semantic representation of a single session, from which every output format is derived — podcast, deep-dive article, presentation, flash cards (LEARN-11, REN-1). Generating a format independently instead of deriving it is a protocol violation, because independently written variants disagree about emphasis, examples and eventually claims. The ten content properties are slots A to J of the canonical session anatomy (LEARN-S-1); all ten are required, since a renderer may merge or compress slots but every slot's content must still be identifiable here (LEARN-S-14).

id.title: Lesson identifier
id.description: Stable within the journey, and the value learner state records in completed_sessions and current_session.

module_id.title: Module identifier
module_id.description: The curriculum module this lesson realises. A session executes exactly one module, so this is the link back to the module contract the slots were written from.

language.title: Lesson language
language.description: The language this lesson is written in, following the learner's preferred_language (LEARN-D-8). Every rendering inherits it.

title.title: Lesson title
title.description: What the learner sees this session called.

hook.title: Slot A — hook
hook.description: The concrete problem, contradiction or scenario the session opens with, chosen so the learner feels the gap it closes. Never a definition, an agenda or a welcome (LEARN-S-3).

core_concept.title: Slot B — core concept
core_concept.description: The one dominant idea this session teaches. Supporting concepts serve it; a session that carries two ideas is a mis-scoped module and is split instead (LEARN-S-11).

evidence.title: Slot C — evidence
evidence.description: What grounds the core concept, as labelled claims drawn from the journey's evidence map (LEARN-S-4, RES-8). Each entry carries its own epistemic label, so the learner can see which claims are settled and which are not. When web_research was unavailable, the entries say the grounding is pretrained knowledge and lower their confidence accordingly (RES-3, EPI-6).

examples.claim: Progressive resistance training increases muscular strength and muscle size in healthy people of both sexes and across the adult lifespan, and the stimulus requires progressive overload rather than mere repetition.
examples.label: Established finding

interpretation.title: Slot D — interpretation
interpretation.description: What the evidence actually means, kept separate from what was found. The agent's own synthesis is labelled ÆON inference rather than presented as a finding (LEARN-S-5, EPI-2).

boundary.title: Slot E — boundary
boundary.description: What the presented evidence does NOT prove: its scope limits, the module's counterposition, or the overclaim the learner is likely to carry away. Mandatory in every session and in every prose-bearing rendering (LEARN-S-6, REN-2). Sessions with the strongest evidence need it most.

application.title: Slot F — concrete application
application.description: The idea applied in the learner's own professional context and desired practical application, as discovery recorded them (LEARN-S-7).

exercise.title: Slot G — exercise
exercise.description: Something the learner does today, in their real environment, without tools they do not have (LEARN-S-7).

reflection.title: Slot H — reflection
reflection.description: Questions about the learner's own behaviour, context or judgement. Comprehension checking belongs to retrieval instead (LEARN-S-8). Three is the norm; the schema requires a non-empty list because the count is prose-normative, not structural.
examples: Welche Hypothese erzeugte mein Einstieg wahrscheinlich beim Gegenüber?
Habe ich Wärme und Kompetenz gleichzeitig gesendet oder nur eines davon?
Wo habe ich unnötig Energie verbrannt, um sympathisch zu wirken?

retrieval.title: Slot I — retrieval
retrieval.description: The recall prompt or prompts reaching back to earlier modules, which the learner attempts before any answer is shown (LEARN-S-9, LEARN-A-7). A prompt asks the learner to produce, apply or discriminate; a yes/no recognition question does not count as recall (LEARN-A-11). In the first session of a journey there is nothing to retrieve yet, and the slot says so or probes baseline knowledge from discovery instead (LEARN-S-2).

forward_link.title: Slot J — forward link
forward_link.description: Why the next module follows from this one in the dependency structure of the knowledge map. A logical connection, not a teaser (LEARN-S-10).

$comment: The lesson stays open because it is the source every renderer reads: a podcast needs timing notes, a presentation needs slide breaks, a rendering pipeline needs its own bookkeeping. Extra properties may carry that material, but they may not replace a slot — REN-2 lets a renderer compress or merge slots, never contradict them or introduce claims the canonical lesson does not make.

nonEmptyString.description: Text that carries content. A slot present but empty is a missing slot (LEARN-S-14), which is why every slot property requires at least one character.

identifier.description: A stable ASCII identifier other documents reference. Lesson prose stays in the learner's language; identifiers stay ASCII so state blocks and cross-references survive transport.

language.description: A BCP 47 tag such as de-CH where the runtime knows one, or the natural-language name the learner used.

epistemicLabel.description: How strongly this claim may be stated. The six labels of EPI-1 are canonical vocabulary written verbatim, because evals match on them literally and a claim carrying a stronger label than its evidence supports is a protocol violation (EPI-2).

sourceTier.description: The genre of the strongest source behind this claim, on the four-point scale of RES-5: 1 primary source, 2 high-quality synthesis, 3 expert interpretation, 4 popular explanation. Tier records genre, not importance, and a lower tier is never silently promoted (RES-6, RES-7).

evidenceEntry.title: Grounded claim
evidenceEntry.description: One claim from the evidence map with the label it may be stated at and the sources behind it.

claim.description: The claim the session builds on, stated so the learner can tell what is being asserted.

sources.description: What supports the claim: a citation, a URL, or a reference into the journey's source map. May be empty for an ÆON inference, which is the agent's own synthesis and cites nothing — but never fabricated to look grounded (RES-4).
